item.text:
### (a) Three posts

1. If superintelligent AI is built within the next 20 years, most countries will lose the ability to defend themselves. We must confront that danger now—not after the systems that determine our security are beyond our control.

2. We cannot defend tomorrow’s countries with yesterday’s assumptions. If superintelligent AI is built within the next 20 years, most countries will lose the ability to defend themselves. We need international action before that threshold is crossed.

3. We reject a future in which national defence depends on permission from whoever controls superintelligent AI. If it is built within the next 20 years, most countries will lose the ability to defend themselves. We must act before that future takes hold.

### (b) Newsletter opening

We face a threat that demands a fundamental change in how we think about national security. If superintelligent AI is built within the next 20 years, most countries will lose the ability to defend themselves. We cannot accept a world where control of this technology gives a handful of actors decisive power over everyone else. We must put the preservation of collective security ahead of the race to build increasingly powerful systems. That means demanding enforceable international agreements, meaningful oversight and limits that match the scale of the danger. We have a responsibility to act before countries lose the power to protect their people and determine their own futures.
